static_traits.name: Wang Jing
static_traits.gender: Female (records inconsistent: self-described as mother, but form marked as male)
static_traits.family_status: Has two daughters; husband works in telecom
static_traits.social_status: Has an interpersonal support network (friend group), but feels uncomfortable sharing motherhood troubles
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems occurred before; has not received psychotherapy/counseling
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic, cooperative; emotions dominated by guilt and self-doubt, neutral attitude

basic_info.main_problem: Because my daughters do not like doing activities like hiking with me, I feel frustrated and not good enough as a mother, and guilty for insisting on activities I enjoy.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent inadequacy and guilt have left me overwhelmed; hoping to ease these feelings, explore more balanced parent-child interaction, and rebuild confidence in motherhood.

core_beliefs: Only by fully catering to the child's interests do I count as qualified

special_situations.event: Daughters clearly stated no interest in hiking and other outdoor adventures
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the children do not like my interests, it means I did something wrong as a mother or am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequently discussing with daughters and trying to get them to join different activities, attempting to prove competence by changing activities
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They do not like hiking with me, which shows I am an incompetent mother

special_situations.event: Whenever planning outdoor activities, anticipating daughters will not be interested
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If they are unwilling to join again, it proves my parenting has failed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing plans or lowering activity intensity, while constantly criticizing self inwardly to avoid being rejected again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will surely hate this plan, and I will be the 'bad mom' again

special_situations.event: When thinking that other mothers in the friend circle 'seem to handle it all well'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I show distress, others will think I have failed at motherhood
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids confiding in friends or seeking support, trying to keep problems bottled up inside
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am a failure, a bad mother

special_situations.event: When family game night makes the whole family happy and connected with each other
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the bond is not built through the outdoor activities I love, it does not count as real mother-daughter closeness
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Belittles the significance of such positive experiences, continuing to demand of herself with high standards that relationships must be built through outdoor means
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This does not count as real closeness, this cannot prove I am doing well

core_conflict.wish: Longing to build an intimate, recognized mother-daughter bond with daughters, feeling needed and accepted in shared activities
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being rejected by daughters, seen as a failed mother, thus losing self-worth
defense_goal: Avoids being judged and rejected through self-blame and people-pleasing
Maintains surface control and restraint, reducing exposure of vulnerability to gain a sense of safety

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, a mother who needs to prove herself
A mother easily compared and appearing failed
object_relations.object_representation: 'Perfect' other mothers / judges in the friend circle

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether they have confided motherhood troubles to friends or thinking of friends 'all handling it well'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing friends look down on her, seeing herself as a failed mother (transference: projecting inner self-criticism onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expresses in a vague, reserved manner, downplaying own needs, avoiding deeply unfolding personal vulnerable experiences.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When daughters refuse or are unwilling to join outdoor activities
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interprets external rejection as own failure and turns to harsh self-blame (transference: internalizing disappointment and frustration)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Respond in an apologetic and self-denying tone, expressing own needs and preferences less.

manifestations: Lack of closeness and sense of distance from differing interests with daughters
Worried about exposing vulnerability among friends, being seen as a failure, and avoiding confiding
outcomes: Decreased parent-child connection, increased subjective sense of isolation

manifestations: Torn between persisting in one's interest (mountaineering) and fulfilling mother-role expectations
Self-demands of 'should': daughters' interests should come first
outcomes: Guilt and self-blame, experiencing restricted freedom of choice
Value conflicts lead to emotional distress and decision hesitation

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequent self-doubt and self-criticism ('I am a bad mom / not good enough')
Restraining expression of troubles in front of relatives and friends, overly cautiously maintaining my image

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Assumes friends will think oneself a failure, so avoids seeking help
Attributing inner shame and self-blame experiences to others' potential judgment

exception_events.target_problem: When building connection with daughters, the client usually tries outdoor adventures (like hiking) as the main way, but daughters are not interested, triggering her frustration, guilt, and self-doubt.
exception_events.unique_outcome: At a specific moment on family game night, everyone felt happy and effectively built parent-child connection, different from past frustrating experiences around outdoor activities.
exception_events.reason: Different situation: choosing activities closer to daughters' interests, lower pressure and more collaborative, making interaction easier and acceptable to daughters.

positive_force: Has stable social support resources (a supportive friend network)
Willing to communicate and try compromise (able to propose gentler options such as picnics and short walks)
Able to notice and seek help (proactively visits for help)
Has successful parent-child interaction experience (family game night)
Love and investment in outdoor activities, which can be converted into resources for shared parent-child experiences
negative_force: Self-worth highly attaches to role norms and external evaluation ('a good mother should...')
Significant cognitive distortions: personalization, mind reading, negating the positive, catastrophizing / overgeneralization
Shame about and avoidance of seeking support (worrying about being seen by friends as a failure)
Interprets differences in interests as relationship failure, weakening the possibility of diverse connections

target_behavior.behavior: Strong guilt and self-doubt when planning parent-child activities (self-blame and negative automatic thoughts recurring)
antecedent: Anticipating daughters' disinterest when planning outdoor activities
After comparison thoughts like 'other mothers all handle it well' arise
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized role belief: a good mother should prioritize children's interests; mismatched interests equal failure
target_behavior.function: Escaping anxiety about being rejected and judged, maintaining surface control and safety
target_behavior.consequence: Reduces the flexibility and satisfaction of parent-child interaction, increases self-blame and frustration, weakens persistence in and sharing of their own interests

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids seeking support from friends or sharing motherhood troubles
antecedent: Thinks of friends as 'all very organized / handling things well'
Being asked whether related topics were discussed with friends
target_behavior.core_reason: Fears that exposing vulnerability will be seen as failure, externalizing inner shame experience as others' potential judgment
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential shame and negating feedback, briefly lowering anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Insufficient use of social support, sense of isolation and negative self-evaluation maintained or worsened
